analysis.title: GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | prime | risk | WWD
key_insights: US S&P futures were up 110bps pre-market, led by NDX up almost 200bps. Asia was mixed: KOSPI +139bps, Taiwan -440bps on short selling curb headlines, Shanghai indices near 52-week lows.

Commodities were flat after the prior day's rout, which the desk attributes to aggressive CTA selling. Oil keeps falling despite a Houthi missile attack that damaged a Riyadh home (per Reuters), because supply concerns dominate.
The 10-year yield is off an elevated 5.08% and the curve is flattening. DXY is just below 104 and Bitcoin is up 2% to $63.7k.
Fed speakers continue to lead hawkish ahead of the December FOMC meeting. Today's calendar: claims, Philly Fed, Fed speakers, Walmart earnings, 10-year TIPS auction at 18:00.

Prime Services: Industrials is the second most net sold US sector month to date, with short and long sales at roughly 2 to 1. Nearly all subsectors are net sold, led by Electrical Equipment, Ground Transportation and Construction & Engineering.

US Industrials net exposure is the lowest in more than 2 years. Medium-term momentum factor exposure is on track to fall for a 6th straight month to the lowest since Dec 2022 (20th percentile over 5 years), while value factor exposure has risen to 5-year highs on stagflation concerns.

Privo on risk: SPX is holding its 200-day moving average. Street gamma positioning is meant to be very short, but vol was soggy the prior day, particularly after VIX expiry. With VIX in the mid 20s and Thanksgiving next week, a stabilization could be a tailwind, and a bull case for equities exists if rates cooperate.
Privo: Watch JPY approaching 160 and broader tech today.

WWD reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $2.83 vs. $2.54 expected, with sales of $1.16bn vs. $1.14bn. Fiscal year ended at 1.6x leverage. EBIT was $236mm vs. $215mm expected, with Aerospace $190mm vs. $187mm and Industrial $79mm vs. $68mm.

WWD fiscal 2027 guidance: sales up 6-10%, EPS $10.20-10.70, FCF $400-450mm, capex $290mm, 60mm shares, 22% tax rate. Aerospace sales growth 8-13% with 23.8-24.3% margins. Industrial sales growth 1-5% with 18.2-18.7% margins. The options market implied a 9% move.
WWD feedback: 25% services growth in fiscal Q4 is a strong base for fiscal 2027, and the desk reads the guide as quite conservative.
CPA reported Q3 EPS of $4.29 vs. $3.74 expected, with revenue of $1.2bn vs. $1.18bn. EBIT was $224mm vs. $190mm and operating margin was 18.6%. The call was at 11am with an 8% implied move.

GIR (Sue Maklari) on Home Depot and Lowe's F3Q results: demand is led by maintenance and small-ticket repair. HD US comps were +2.2% y/y vs +0.1% a year earlier, with gains in 13 of 16 departments. LOW comps were +1.8% vs +0.4%, with 7 of 13 categories up.

GIR attributes weaker-than-expected demand into year-end to mortgage rates above 7% and macro uncertainty, while price and mix improve as manufacturers offset inflation. GIR highlights Buy-rated FBIN, MAS, MHK and TREX as best positioned.
GIR (Catie O'Brien) hosted a virtual roundtable on AI and travel covering how consumers plan and book travel, industry economics, and AI as an operational and revenue opportunity.

tension_points.bull_case: Privo says a stabilizing market, with VIX in the mid 20s and Thanksgiving next week, could produce a tailwind, and that much of the AI concern is already in price. A bull case exists if rates cooperate.
tension_points.bear_case: SPX is only just holding its 200-day moving average, the 10-year is near 5.08%, and Fed speakers lead hawkish ahead of the December FOMC meeting.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break of the SPX 200-day moving average, or rates that fail to cooperate.
